title: Member-Owner Relief on the Rural Home Loans Returned-Payment Fee
content:
**Member-owner benefit.** As a cooperative, the association gives its member-owners relief on the returned-payment fee of a Rural Home Loans loan, decided from the member's Member Equities & Patronage records.

## Tiers

A member-owner earns relief on the fee: a member whose Class B Voting Stock is active and who was paid cash patronage in the 15 months up to today has 40 percent of the fee taken off; a member whose Class B Voting Stock is active but who was paid no cash patronage in those 15 months has 20 percent taken off; any other member earns no relief.

## Records read on the Member Equities & Patronage side

- The member's Class B Voting Stock holding and whether its status is active.
- Cash patronage payments booked to the member in the 15 months up to today, from the day after the same calendar day 15 months before today through today.

## How the relief acts

The relief percentage is taken off once, from the fee as limited by the size of the returned remittance, and the returned-payment fee is the result rounded to the cent, rounded only at the end.

## Truth table

| Class B Voting Stock active | Cash patronage paid in the 15 months | Relief |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | 40 percent |
| yes | no | 20 percent |
| no, or no Class B Voting Stock | — | none |

A member who holds a Class C Participation Certificate or Class A Nonvoting Common Stock and no active Class B Voting Stock earns no relief, whatever patronage was paid.

## Worked figures (hypothetical inputs)

A fee of 35.00 for a member with active Class B Voting Stock and cash patronage paid 11 months ago: 40 percent taken off leaves 21.00. Without patronage in the 15 months: 20 percent taken off leaves 28.00.
